sections.title: In the dental chair
items: Diabetes raises the risk and severity of periodontal disease, delays wound healing, invites oral infections and causes xerostomia; the dentist may be the first to suspect it.
Ask what insulin was taken and whether the patient ate: a rapid-acting dose without a meal is the classic set-up for hypoglycemia.
Awake and able to swallow: orange juice, regular soda or glucose tablets. Unresponsive: glucagon (injection kit, stable liquid or nasal).
Secretagogues (glipizide, glyburide, glimepiride, repaglinide, nateglinide) and insulin cause hypoglycemia; metformin, DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT2 inhibitors, TZDs and GLP-1 agonists alone rarely do.
Patients on an SGLT2 inhibitor may be dizzy or hypotensive when the chair is brought upright (osmotic diuresis).
GLP-1 agonists slow gastric emptying, which can delay the absorption of an antibiotic you prescribe or an oral contraceptive.
Sulfonylureas: a disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol, as with metronidazole.

sections.title: Drug interactions to remember
items: GLP-1 agonists: delayed gastric emptying slows drugs that need rapid absorption (oral contraceptives, antibiotics).
Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors: less digoxin absorbed with acarbose; less propranolol and ranitidine with miglitol.
Colesevelam: less warfarin, phenytoin, verapamil, glyburide, thyroxine, ethinyl estradiol and fat-soluble vitamins absorbed.
Sulfonylureas: disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol.

sections.title: Thyroid tumor histology, in words
items: Follicular adenoma: normal-appearing follicles inside an intact fibrous capsule; no invasion.
Follicular carcinoma: an encapsulated tumor pushing through its capsule (mushroom-like) or sitting inside a vessel lined by endothelium.
Papillary carcinoma: papillae on fibrovascular cores; enlarged, overcrowded, pale nuclei (Orphan Annie eye) with grooves and pseudoinclusions; laminated psammoma bodies in half.
Medullary carcinoma: solid nests of somewhat spindled neuroendocrine cells, no colloid, amyloid with apple-green birefringence; brown for calcitonin, chromogranin and CEA.
Anaplastic carcinoma: high-grade nuclei, high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, resembles no tissue, may lose thyroid markers.
Hashimoto thyroiditis: many lymphocytes; follicular cells with larger, irregular nuclei and pinker cytoplasm.
Graves disease: diffuse hyperplasia of the follicular cells throughout the gland.

sections.title: Hypopituitarism: causes and signs
items: Appears after about 75 percent of the anterior pituitary is lost; less often a hypothalamic disorder blocks the releasing factors.
Causes: null cell (non-secretory) adenoma, Sheehan syndrome (postpartum ischemic necrosis), ablation, empty sella syndrome (obese multiparous women), inflammation, trauma, metastases.

Signs: fatigue, weight loss, low sex drive, cold sensitivity, low appetite, facial puffiness, anemia, infertility; in women hot flashes, absent periods, loss of pubic hair, no milk; in men less facial and body hair.
